finding.preliminary_assessment: The getCss() regex filter for blocking url(), expression(), and javascript: patterns has two identified bypass vectors: (1) CSS comment injection — the regex uses \s* between 'url' and '(' but CSS comment sequences (/**/) are not whitespace and are not consumed by \s*, so 'url/**/(' passes the regex unmatched; (2) CSS hex escape encoding — 'jav\61script:' uses CSS hex escape where \61 = 'a', but the browser normalizes this at render time to 'javascript:'. If Angular's [style] binding passes values to the browser DOM without normalization, the escape would be evaluated. Both bypasses exist in both FieldComponent and InputFieldComponent. The allowlist (ALLOWED_CSS_PROPS) itself is conservative and well-designed — this issue is specifically in the value-level regex filter. Impact: compromised ApplinX backend could inject CSS that loads external resources, exfiltrates data via CSS-based sidechannel, or (via expression()) executes code in legacy browsers.
